diagnosis.reason: All train episodes were won but with wasted exploration steps (e.g., 9-10 searches before finding the object). Adding goal-type plan templates, likely-location search order, open-before-give-up, and one-instance-at-a-time sequencing should shorten unseen episodes and avoid partial two-object tasks, without changing any successful patterns.

The lost episode burned its entire step budget walking through cabinets without opening them and never retrieved the kettle. Adding task-type pipelines, likely-location search order, mandatory open-after-arrive for closed receptacles, and already-located skip rules should cut wasted exploration steps on unseen episodes of all goal types.

The lost kettle episode spent 20 steps searching cabinets before checking tables, then ran out of steps right after cleaning without placing the object. Adding likely-location search order, mandatory open-after-go for closed receptacles, task-type pipelines, and an explicit finish-placement-under-step-pressure rule should cut wasted exploration steps and prevent episodes ending with the goal object still in inventory.

The lost episode exhausted its budget opening cabinet after cabinet without reserving steps for cleaning and delivery. Adding open-before-contents awareness, likely-first search order, step budgeting with a reserved delivery phase, no-revisit rule, and goal-type pipelines should cut wasted exploration and ensure tasks finish within the step limit on unseen episodes.
